gaps.note: Unrolling Q_k <= (s/W) Q_{k-1} + C gives a plus C times the geometric sum, not a minus. The reader who unrolls the displayed recurrence gets a different formula, and the page never says why the sign is negative, so the step cannot be checked.

gaps.quote: The geometric sum is also $O(m^{k\tau})$, since it is $O((s/W)^k)$.
gaps.note: A geometric sum with ratio s/W is O((s/W)^k) only if s/W > 1. The page never says s/W > 1; if s/W < 1 the sum is O(1) and if s/W = 1 it is k. The reader cannot check which case applies.
The page never states or justifies m >= 2 (m is only a cited growth factor), and does not explain how m >= 2 turns the bounds into O(m^{k tau}), for example for the O(1) term.
